newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil BNDES and CVRD sign risk contract.
newsitem.headline: Brazil BNDES and CVRD sign risk contract.

text.p: The presidents of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) and state mining giant CVRD have signed a risk contract giving each the right to 50 percent of the mineral wealth found after CVRD's privatization.

The contract applies to future mineral finds in the Carajas mining region in the northern state of Para, which holds the largest iron ore deposit in the world and is rich in other minerals such as gold, silver, copper and manganese.
The risk contract was introduced as part of the privatization process of CVRD, after critics accused the government of selling off future untold mineral wealth for a pittance.

"This contract preserves the interests of the Treasury in the future mineral riches which could not be included in the minimum price for CVRD because they haven't been evaluated yet," said BNDES President Luiz Carlos Mendonca de Barros.
The risk contract ensures the government retains its right to 50 percent of CVRD's future mineral finds in Carajas via the BNDES participation in the contract.
A 45 percent voting stake in CVRD will be sold at a privatization auction April 29 for 3 billion reais ($2.83 billion) as a first step in the privatization of the company.
A staff and global offering will complete the process of selling off the government's entire 51 percent stake in CVRD, expected to net a total of at least 5 billion reais ($4.72 billion).

Under the contract, BNDES and CVRD will jointly invest more than 400 million reais ($377.4 million) over the next five years to carry out research and evaluate 104 areas where CVRD has already identified potential mineral reserves, Barros said.
He said CVRD had already invested more than 100 million reais ($94.3 million) of the 200 million reais ($188.7 million) it is set to invest under the contract.

Under the deal, BNDES or CVRD can sell or acquire the other's 50 percent stake if one is not interested in continuing with the research and exploration of reserves included in the contract, said CVRD President Francisco Schettino.
He said once a prospect in the areas covered by the risk contract is being mined, a finder's fee of 6.5 percent on turnover will be paid to CVRD shareholders.
